cards.name: AI_Alpha_1
cards.summary: Masks the artwork with a two-octave turbulence pattern (feTurbulence, base frequency 0.05, composited 'in'): colours stay but the object turns mostly see-through, a pale cloud of soft mottled blotches; strokes are mottled the same way (on the test plate the box outline and the zigzag kept their full width, only paler).
use_for: distressed / worn-print texture on a badge or stamp graphic
cloudy see-through fill for a web SVG background shape
grunge treatment on large display shapes
avoid: Small text or fine line art: the blotches eat legibility; use an opacity mask with a texture you control instead.
Its amounts are fixed numbers in document units with no sliders, so they do not grow with a big artboard or a scaled object.

Listed only while the document holds this filter definition (new-document profiles ship it); a file opened from elsewhere may lack it: use Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter or Apply SVG Filter first.
Keep it the last effect in the Appearance stack: effects added after an SVG filter make SVG export write a raster instead of the live <filter>.

cards.name: AI_Dilate_3
cards.summary: Grows the artwork by 3 units on every side (feMorphology dilate, radius 3, per colour channel): shapes and type fatten, corners square off, small gaps and counters tighten, and where two colours meet the brighter channels win (a red fill against a blue stroke turns magenta at the seam).
use_for: make thin type or a hairline icon heavier without editing paths
fatten a silhouette for a sticker die-cut border
close small gaps in traced line art
avoid: Clean, rounded expansion of vector paths: use Effect/Path/Offset Path or a thicker stroke; this is raster-style and squares the corners.
Artwork where adjacent colours must stay pure: the per-channel max mixes them at the seams.

The definition sets no filter region, so the SVG default (object bounds plus 10% each side) applies: on thin or small objects (a rule, a short word) the spread can be cut off in a straight line; group the art with a larger no-fill rectangle and apply it to the group, or use Effect/Blur/Gaussian Blur.
Its amounts are fixed numbers in document units with no sliders, so they do not grow with a big artboard or a scaled object.

Listed only while the document holds this filter definition (new-document profiles ship it); a file opened from elsewhere may lack it: use Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter or Apply SVG Filter first.

cards.name: AI_Erode_3
cards.summary: Shrinks the artwork by 3 units from every edge (feMorphology erode, radius 3, per channel): shapes and type thin, stand-alone strokes 6 units or thinner vanish, and where colours meet the per-channel minimum wins, so a stroke on a fill becomes a near-black band (a red fill with a blue stroke gives near-black, not blue).
use_for: lighten the weight of bold type or icons without editing paths
pull fills back from an edge for a slight inset look
clean small specks off traced artwork
avoid: Artwork with hairlines or thin strokes: they disappear; use Effect/Path/Offset Path with a negative offset on the fill instead.
Exact vector insets for print: this works on pixels with a square kernel, not on the path.
Multi-colour artwork: every seam between two colours turns dark (per-channel minimum), so coloured strokes become near-black outlines.
Its amounts are fixed numbers in document units with no sliders, so they do not grow with a big artboard or a scaled object.

Listed only while the document holds this filter definition (new-document profiles ship it); a file opened from elsewhere may lack it: use Effect > SVG Filters > Import SVG Filter or Apply SVG Filter first.
